hello.note: Works any time of day. The formal version is ជំរាបសួរ (chum-reap-suor), said with palms together

good-morning.text: អរុណសួស្តី
good-morning.note: Rather formal; soo-sdei alone is fine all day

good-night.text: រាត្រីសួស្តី
good-night.note: Formal. At bedtime people often say គេងលក់ស្រួល (keng luk sruol), sleep well

please.note: Goes before a request: soum + what you want

thank-you.note: អរគុណច្រើន (aw-kohn chraeun) means thank you very much

yes.note: What men say. Women say ចាស (chaas)

dont-understand.text: ខ្ញុំមិនយល់ទេ

speak-slowly.text: សូមនិយាយយឺតៗ
speak-slowly.note: Saying a word twice, as in yeut yeut, softens it

repeat.text: សូមនិយាយម្តងទៀត

speak-english.text: តើអ្នកចេះនិយាយអង់គ្លេសទេ
speak-english.say: tae neak chess nee-yeay ong-kleh teh
speak-english.note: តើ at the start and ទេ at the end mark a yes/no question. អ្នក (neak) means you

five.note: Counting from six goes five-one, five-two, and so on

thousand.note: Prices are in riel or US dollars. 4,000 riel is about one dollar

hundred-thousand.note: Khmer has its own word, សែន (saen), for a hundred thousand

how-much.text: ថ្លៃប៉ុន្មាន
how-much.note: Point at the item and say នេះថ្លៃប៉ុន្មាន (nih t'lay pon-man), how much is this?

would-like.note: Literally "I ask for …"; the polite way to order

i-want.text: ខ្ញុំចង់បាន…

do-you-have.text: តើអ្នកមាន…ទេ
do-you-have.note: Put the item in the gap. The audio uses water as the example
do-you-have.spoken: តើអ្នកមានទឹកទេ

just-looking.text: ខ្ញុំគ្រាន់តែមើល

ill-take-it.text: ខ្ញុំយកនេះ

discount.text: បញ្ចុះតម្លៃបានទេ
discount.note: Bargaining is normal in markets, not in fixed-price shops

card.text: តើអ្នកទទួលកាតទេ
card.note: Cash is still common, and US dollars are accepted in most places

bill.note: គិតលុយ (kit luy) alone also works

reservation.text: ខ្ញុំបានកក់បន្ទប់

checkout-time.text: ត្រូវចេញម៉ោងប៉ុន្មាន

breakfast.text: តើរួមបញ្ចូលអាហារពេលព្រឹកទេ
breakfast.say: tae roo-um ban-jol a-har pel pruk teh

wifi.text: លេខសម្ងាត់វ៉ាយហ្វាយជាអ្វី

toilet.text: បន្ទប់ទឹកនៅឯណា
toilet.note: "… នៅឯណា (nov ae nah)" means "where is …?" for anything

taxi.text: សូមហៅតាក់ស៊ីឲ្យខ្ញុំបានទេ
taxi.say: soum how tak-see ow k'nyom ban teh
taxi.note: Tuk-tuks are more common than taxis, and you can hail one on the street

airport.text: ព្រលានយន្តហោះ

bus-station.text: ចំណតឡានក្រុង

train-station.text: ស្ថានីយរថភ្លើង

where-train-station.text: ស្ថានីយរថភ្លើងនៅឯណា
where-train-station.say: sa-than-ee rot pleung nov ae nah

where-bus-station.text: ចំណតឡានក្រុងនៅឯណា
where-bus-station.say: chom-not lan krong nov ae nah

which-train.text: រថភ្លើងមួយណាទៅ…
which-train.note: មួយណា (moo-ey nah) means which one. Swap in any city; the audio uses ហាណូយ (Hanoi) as the example
which-train.spoken: រថភ្លើងមួយណាទៅហាណូយ

buy-ticket.text: ទិញសំបុត្រនៅឯណា

two-tickets.text: ខ្ញុំសុំទិញសំបុត្រពីរសន្លឹកទៅ…
two-tickets.say: k'nyom som tin sam-bot pee son-leuk tov …
two-tickets.note: សន្លឹក (son-leuk) counts tickets. The audio uses ហាណូយ (Hanoi) as the example
two-tickets.spoken: ខ្ញុំសុំទិញសំបុត្រពីរសន្លឹកទៅហាណូយ

trip-length.text: ទៅ…ចំណាយពេលប៉ុន្មាន
trip-length.note: The audio uses ហាណូយ (Hanoi) as the example
trip-length.spoken: ទៅហាណូយចំណាយពេលប៉ុន្មាន

delicious.text: ឆ្ងាញ់ណាស់
delicious.note: Said to the cook, it is a lovely compliment

allergic.text: ខ្ញុំអាឡែរហ្ស៊ីនឹង…
allergic.note: Add the food, or show a note written in Khmer to be safe

love-dish.text: ខ្ញុំចូលចិត្តម្ហូបនេះណាស់
love-dish.note: ចូលចិត្ត (chol-chet) means like, and is the natural word for food. ស្រលាញ់ (sro-lanh) is for people

what-called.text: នេះហៅថាអ្វី
what-called.note: Point at the dish or item

table-for-two.text: ខ្ញុំសុំតុមួយសម្រាប់ពីរនាក់
table-for-two.say: k'nyom som tok moo-ey som-rap pee neak
table-for-two.note: For more people replace ពីរ (pee, two) with បី (bay, three) or បួន (boo-un, four)

menu.text: សុំមើលម៉ឺនុយបានទេ

recommend.text: តើអ្នកណែនាំម្ហូបអ្វី

beer.text: ខ្ញុំសុំបៀរមួយដប
beer.note: Angkor is the local beer. Ask for it by name

coffee.note: កាហ្វេទឹកកក (ka-feh tuk kok) is iced coffee

water.note: Ask for ទឹកសុទ្ធ (tuk sot), bottled drinking water

sugar.note: មិនដាក់ស្ករ (min dak skaw) means without sugar

cheers.note: Literally "clink one". The usual toast as the glasses touch

help.text: ជួយខ្ញុំផង

pharmacy.text: ឱសថស្ថាននៅឯណា
